acceptance.statement: **AC-01 — Complete census (ASSET-02):** Every one of the 180 registered IDs maps to actual inspectable outputs or explicitly declared shared outputs. All required resource families exist; file/atlas/recording counts do not substitute for obligation coverage.

**AC-02 — Exact origins (ASSET-01):** Each selected recovered output/logic unit identifies its owning source file, type, object ID/name or original code unit, preserved-original identity and selected dependencies. Original recovered files remain unchanged.

**AC-03 — Reusable production records (ASSET-01):** Stable output IDs, relative paths, versions/content identities, transformations or Codex/GPT generation sources/recipes and applicable image/audio/animation metadata are recorded. Actual production validation is distinguished from original V/M/C inspection evidence.

**AC-04 — Live composed animation (ASSET-03):** In the Godot character inspector, the reviewer switches bodies, equipment, movement and attacks live. Walking continues during melee, bow aim and firing. Changes appear immediately, clear old visuals and may restart the current animation cleanly. Required combinations do not depend on separately baked full-combination sheets.

**AC-05 — Required body/equipment coverage (ASSET-02/03):** The survivor and all seven recognizable zombie silhouettes support every applicable item, direction and required AN action, including wide bodies, clothing, both armor types, belt, gloves, boots and both backpacks. All 24 item definitions have identifiable icons and applicable worn/held forms. Only AC-18's bounded cosmetic exceptions may remain.

**AC-06 — Hands, ammunition and condition (ASSET-03):** Fixtures show fists, either-hand one-handed weapons, mixed dual attacks, bow/arrow states, empty/changed arrow hands and broken/fallback gear. Facing changes preserve logical inventory hand identity; visible equipment/ammunition reflects the selected sample state.

**AC-07 — Corpses and loot (ASSET-03):** Ordinary survivor/zombie and rabbit/deer corpse endpoints remain inspectable/selectable after effects fade. Changing the sample remaining equipment updates the corpse appearance, crown loss is represented, and nonempty/empty/selected states are distinguishable. Structural guards produce no character corpse or item loot.

**AC-08 — Buildings and portals (ASSET-03):** Fixtures show all three main/wall/tower tiers and required site, frame, upgrade, damage, repair, destruction, previous-tier/rebuild and permanent portal-ruin states. Standalone tiers show 1/2/3 independently animated guards; main tier 3 has exactly two one-guard attachments. Upgrades preserve the visible old functional tier until completion.

**AC-09 — World and crowd resources (ASSET-02/03):** The assembled map contains the baseline six portals, eight wall/eight standalone-tower sites, clearing groups, six food plants, wildlife zones, terrain and interaction/navigation/collision metadata. Day/night, plant/clearing/prey/effect states are inspectable. Short crowd/persistent-corpse fixtures use the real presentation resources for approximately 100 survivors/300 zombies and the later ≥200 nonempty-corpse/pile scenario; no FPS or three-hour endurance pass is inferred.

**AC-10 — UI state resources (ASSET-04):** UI-01–UI-27 and their required normal, empty, waiting, disabled, invalid, conflicting, legacy, lost-access and failure examples are present as reusable layouts/state resources. These examples can be inspected without implementing their future gameplay interaction logic.

**AC-11 — Text, scale and identity (ASSET-04):** TXT-01/02 cover all specified labels/descriptions/prompts/errors and preserve formatting placeholders/current-binding references. Layout examples demonstrate supported resolutions/scales, longer replacement text, readable names/numbers/counts and four identities distinguishable beyond color. Held-out display/text cases are carried by AC-19.

**AC-12 — Auditioned sound (ASSET-04):** AU-01–AU-30 map to auditioned recordings or generated replacements with documented event routing, duration/channel/rate/trim/loop/gain and mix/priority/repetition settings. Day/night and local ambience can be auditioned, baseline 24/four limits are configurable, and critical warnings have visible examples when muted.

**AC-13 — Complete data/support (ASSET-04):** DT-01–DT-27 are present with the complete working baseline, documented meanings/units/defaults/allowed values/dependencies and representative editing examples. Item/content/image/sound/text references validate, zombie progression is independently editable, and local preferences are separated from host balance.

**AC-14 — Compatibility presentation (ASSET-03/04):** Stable IDs/versions and sample saved-layout/appearance metadata support inspectable old grid dimensions/placements/orientation, incompatible slots/stacks/depth, current-destination previews and explicit missing-definition errors. Fixture restoration shows persistent gear/corpses/ruins/loops without replaying past one-shot effects; actual gameplay save/load and extraction remain later integration.

**AC-15 — Windows content delivery (ASSET-05):** The Godot project, inspection scenes and Windows inspection build load their selected content, fonts, text, data and audio without the external recovery folder or absolute development-path dependencies. Source-locator text in provenance does not create a runtime dependency.

**AC-16 — Visible incomplete state (ASSET-05):** Deliberately absent/invalid required resources identify the exact resource ID/path and problem, mark the pack incomplete and leave unaffected gallery entries inspectable. A fallback display cannot turn a missing required output into completed coverage.

**AC-17 — Focused current evidence (ASSET-05):** Documented focused Windows import/export/launch, content, visual and audio checks provide current results and required diagnostic evidence. Missing evidence is recorded as such. Linux execution, broad build matrices, full gameplay and release performance/endurance are not claimed from this inspection run.

**AC-18 — Bounded cosmetic carryover (ASSET-02/03):** Every remaining known issue is a reproducible minor cosmetic flaw in an exactly documented uncommon combination; all required gear/actions/critical states remain readable. The register records expected/actual results and a Phase 6/7/8 owner as specified above. A missing resource or non-cosmetic required-state failure blocks Phase 4 completion.

**AC-19 — Held-out edges (ASSET-01–05):** Planning carries all 34 Edge Coverage rows into non-inferable must-have checks, and Phase 4 obtains held-out evidence for them. Inputs/combinations are chosen independently of authored happy-path examples. Cases may share setup/evidence when their individual obligations remain identifiable; these are not 34 separate build runs. Any unsupported backstop remains a visible verification gap.

**AC-20 — Inspection boundary (ASSET-03–05):** The delivered resource index and inspection entry points expose the live character controls, assembled map, UI state examples, data and audio described here. Resource inspection is clearly identified; the pack's completion record does not claim implementation of the later gameplay interactions or a complete playable campaign.

**AC-21 — Blood limit (ASSET-02/03, prohibition):** Hit/death presentation uses restrained blood effects and MUST NOT include dismemberment. Verify by recorded visual judgment across the relevant effect/death families.

**AC-22 — Honest provenance/status (ASSET-01/02, prohibition):** Production records MUST NOT present catalog entries/metadata/unfinished exports as completed assets or label generated/adapted material as unchanged donor reuse. Verify through recorded source/output and evidence-status review.

**AC-23 — Game identity (ASSET-02/04/05, prohibition):** Title, icon and UI identify KingdomZombies and MUST NOT use Kingdom Two Crowns or publisher logos as the game's identity. Verify by recorded visual review.

**AC-24 — Truthful mechanic presentation (ASSET-03/04, prohibition):** Art/UI MUST NOT imply recoverable fired arrows, lootable dropped crowns, structural-guard loot, damaging bloater acid or an active-game menu that pauses play. Donor visuals follow KingdomZombies' specified mechanics. Verify by recorded visual/content review.

heldout.sourceIntent: H01: Same-named donors in different owning files/types and explicitly shared outputs retain the right source/output identities; AC-02/03/19.
H02: A selected output with missing origin, identity, recipe or required evidence cannot obtain completed provenance; AC-03/19.
H03: Case/encoding variants cannot silently alias stable IDs/source locators or portable paths; AC-02/03/19.
H04: Reordering donor/manifest enumeration preserves exact output-to-origin resolution; AC-02/03/19.
H05: Interrupted/competing production work preserves originals and cannot publish unvalidated output as verified; AC-02/03/19.
H06: A missing unique obligation remains a failure even when duplicate rows inflate the apparent total to 180; AC-01/19.
H07: Explicitly shared files may satisfy several obligations without collapsing distinct item/resource identities; AC-01/19.
H08: Empty/partial packs and absent or empty required output dependencies cannot count as completed coverage; AC-01/19.
H09: Shuffling resource/mapping order preserves the actual covered-ID set and completeness result; AC-01/19.
H10: Unique integer obligation coverage is exact; percentages, duplicate files or rounding cannot certify an incomplete pack; AC-01/19.
H11: Output generation/import interrupted partway through remains visibly incomplete rather than gaining metadata-only coverage; AC-01/16/19.
H12: Empty/last-arrow and broken/usable transitions, required tier/guard counts and persistent-corpse boundaries preserve the intended presentation; AC-06/07/08/19.
H13: Overlapping coat/armor/belt/bag/hand layers and nearby bodies keep required gear and target identity readable; AC-05/07/18/19.
H14: Empty hands/ammunition/slots, empty versus nonempty corpses and the structural-guard exception do not invent equipment or loot; AC-06/07/19.
H15: Facing/action/gear order changes retain correct final equipment, occlusion and logical hand identity; AC-04/05/06/19.
H16: Donor pixel registration, offsets, nonuniform frame timing, held/repeated frames and loop/endpoints survive conversion/composition; AC-03/04/05/19.
H17: Repeated preview reset/state restoration leaves one current composition/loop/corpse state without replaying past one-shots; AC-04/07/14/19.
H18: Mid-action body/gear changes immediately clear replaced visuals, permit a clean restart and retain concurrent walking/combat presentation; AC-04/19.
H19: Supported resolution/UI-scale endpoints, expanded text and configured sound limits remain inspectable; AC-11/12/19.
H20: Equal labels/values and touching/overlapping UI or legacy-grid regions do not merge identities or hide critical warning/state information; AC-10/11/14/19.
H21: Empty/zero-result examples and missing/invalid text, audio or data refs show the right state/diagnostic without a false resource pass; AC-10/11/12/13/19.
H22: Catalog encoding, exact IDs/placeholders, accented names/font fallback and longer strings remain readable without corrupting text identity; AC-11/19.
H23: Reordered data/definitions retain bindings and quantities; warning layers and four-player identities remain correct across UI state examples; AC-10/11/13/19.
H24: Display scaling, formatting and media conversion do not silently change authored units/defaults, quantities, timing or sound metadata; AC-03/11/12/13/19.
H25: Repeated UI/audio/current-state example restoration does not accumulate ambience loops or replay old transactional/death/warning cues; AC-12/14/19.
H26: Rapid view/audition/state changes leave correct bindings/current loops and visible muted warnings, without requiring later gameplay interactions; AC-10/12/14/19.
H27: Similar/conflicting resource paths are diagnosed accurately; one bad entry does not conceal independent valid entries; AC-15/16/19.
H28: An empty or partially missing pack/gallery cannot obtain a successful content result through zero discovery or fallback art; AC-16/17/19.
H29: Packaged path/ID spelling and readable exact diagnostics do not depend on development-path aliases or encoding loss; AC-15/16/19.
H30: Validation/discovery order cannot suppress known resource failures or prevent inspection of unaffected entries; AC-16/19.
H31: Repeated clean launch/close/relaunch uses the same packaged content and does not require hidden donor/editor caches; AC-15/17/19.
H32: Partial imports, interrupted checks or failed launch attempts cannot inherit an earlier successful result; unaffected content remains inspectable where the build can run; AC-16/17/19.
H33 (manual): Re-export/re-import preserves stable selected-output identities without duplicate provenance records; AC-03/19.
H34 (manual): Recomputing or regenerating coverage cannot count one obligation twice or change completeness solely through repetition; AC-01/19.

decisions.statement: **D-01:** Use deliberate pixel-art poses for walking and attacks, with flexible arm/weapon movement where aiming needs it. Keep crisp pixel edges and the required concurrent walking/combat presentation; do not make full baked sheets for every equipment/action combination.
**D-02:** Melee attacks have clear weight and follow-through. Shoulders and torso support the strike; heavier bodies and weapons feel weighty, while quick attacks remain sharp. Walking continues.
**D-03:** Clothing, belts and bags follow their attachment points closely, with little independent sway or bounce. This selects mostly fixed gear rather than the proposed secondary-motion treatment.

**D-04:** Melee effects are very minimal. Let the swing and target reaction carry the action; use only the small contact effects needed for clarity. The restrained-blood/no-dismemberment limit remains binding.
**D-05:** Bow aiming is led mainly by the arms and bow. Keep the head and torso close to their normal pose while aiming up/down, rather than adding pronounced torso/head tracking.
**D-06:** Death uses a short authored collapse suited to each body, ending in a stable, readable equipped corpse pose. A variable physical-collapse treatment was not selected.
**D-07:** Hits cause a small, clear shoulder/torso flinch. This is visual feedback only and adds no stun, knockback or action delay.

**D-08:** Use Godot's built-in animation tools and project code only, with no paid animation dependency. Research and planning should solve composition within that boundary rather than schedule a paid-add-on comparison or purchase.
**D-09:** Direction changes switch facing immediately and continue the current stride/action coherently. Preserve logical left/right hand identity and actual equipment.
**D-10:** Starting to walk uses a quick visual weight shift; stopping uses a short settle. Actual movement starts and stops immediately.

**D-11:** Clothing, armor and bags have a practical scavenged fit: slightly loose, utilitarian and modestly bulky, fitted to each required body. Slightly loose shapes do not imply the independent sway/bounce rejected in D-03.
**D-12:** Gathering, building, carrying and fireside rest use restrained, recognizable task poses with only the body movement each activity needs.

**D-13:** Favor the recovered sprites' simpler, low-resolution logical detail. Simplify the larger zombie/base examples to match, rather than raising the whole pack to their richer detail. Exact pixel density and dimensions remain a research/production choice established through the required assembled survivor/zombie/wall/tower/base scale test.

**D-14:** Use natural days and atmospheric nights: earthy scenery and warm wood in daylight, cooler/darker nights and restrained warm firelight. Required equipment, identities and states remain readable after dark.
**D-15:** Keep character heads, hands and equipment close to natural proportions. Use pose and contrast for readability rather than noticeably enlarged heads/hands/items.

**D-16:** Buildings and defenses look like practical camp construction: rough timber, straightforward bracing and functional reinforcement, with clear tier silhouettes. Preserve the specified wood/reinforced-wood/metal progression.
**D-17:** Backgrounds are layered but unobtrusive. Distant scenery and parallax provide depth while quiet space keeps characters, equipment and sites clear.
**D-18:** For normal unselected characters, strengthen dark outer pixel edges selectively where needed while keeping donor-style shading. Do not apply a uniform outline by default.

**D-19:** Standing damaged structures show localized material damage: cracks, splintered timber, bent reinforcement and small damaged areas, increasing with severity. Keep tier, material and functional state clear.

**D-20:** Provide one canonical inventory icon per item, without separate durability-level icon variants. The creator did not choose one of the proposed icon-art treatments and does not want that detail expanded now. Exact durability indicators remain a planning detail within the required layouts/state examples; this does not remove item identities or required broken/condition presentation, nor the separate worn/held/corpse forms.
**D-21:** Zombie bodies share related muted undead skin tones, with subtle color differences supporting their required distinct silhouettes. Equipped items retain their actual appearance.

**D-22:** Start portal colors from suitable recovered donor colors. Spit and cosmetic acid use separate restrained sickly colors. No exact hue or numeric palette was selected; cosmetic acid remains non-damaging.
**D-23:** Use small, quiet pixel contact-shadow shapes beneath characters and small objects to establish their contact with the ground.

**D-24:** Selected corpses, loot piles and other inspectable objects use a steady thin contrasting pixel outline and modest marker. This defines selected-state presentation; it does not implement later gameplay interactions.

**D-25:** Use one Windows inspection hub organized by category, with common navigation for characters, items, buildings/world, UI, data/text and audio. The complete obligation register and exact resource failures remain accessible under the specification.

**D-26:** The live character page gives one character most of the space, with body, equipment, movement and attack controls alongside. Side-by-side or multi-character comparison layouts were not selected.

**D-27:** Include play/pause, playback-speed and single-step controls to examine grips, layering, poses and timing. These operate the inspection preview; they do not change the active-game menu's no-pause rule.

**D-28:** Keep each preview's resource ID, name and status visible in a compact summary. Expand provenance, dimensions, timing and other metadata when needed. Missing/invalid-resource errors remain visible rather than being hidden in collapsed details.
**D-29:** Use suitable recovered wooden buttons/borders as frames around simple dark, quiet panel interiors. Keep text, numbers and item grids clear.

**D-30:** Use a clear sans-serif face for most body text and numbers, with pixel-style type for selected headings/accents. Exact font files, sizes and fallbacks remain subject to extraction/comparison and the specified readability/scaling/expanded-text checks.

**D-31:** Sound effects are punchier and more game-like: sharper swings, stronger impacts and more noticeable confirmations. This is an explicit selection over the proposed restrained-audio recommendation; the minimal visual-effects preference does not make the audio equally restrained. Suitable recovered recordings still come first and require audition/adaptation.

**D-32:** Keep forest, wind and fire ambience subdued so action sounds and important cues stand out. Include the required day/night/local ambience and audition controls; exact gains and mix parameters remain configurable production choices.

prohibitions.statement: MUST NOT present catalog entries/metadata/unfinished exports as completed assets, or label generated/adapted material as unchanged donor reuse.
MUST NOT use Kingdom Two Crowns or publisher logos as the title/icon/UI identity of KingdomZombies.
MUST NOT imply recoverable fired arrows, lootable dropped crowns, structural-guard loot, damaging bloater acid or an active-game menu that pauses play.
MUST NOT include dismemberment; blood presentation remains restrained.
